policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: The ASV wording 'upon earth' does not distinguish the qere עֲלֵי from the ketiv על. The note is classed alternative_rendering and therefore does not decide the textual reading; both candidates remain compatible, with the qere retained as the base fallback.

The ASV wording 'clods of dust' does not distinguish the qere וְג֣וּשׁ from the ketiv וגיש. The note is classed alternative_rendering and therefore does not decide the textual reading; both candidates remain compatible, with the qere retained as the base fallback.
